Why apply to Global Academy?
Global Academy offers a unique academic and practical opportunity for a limited number of Year 10 – Year 12 students looking to enter the radio, TV, digital, advertising, and social media industries.
From classroom and studio training to work experience and mentorship opportunities with industry professionals, our students receive everything they need to kickstart their careers.
Our alumni have gone on to achieve success in their chosen fields, and many have secured employment with top companies like Global, the BBC, and Sky. By working with these and other leading employers, we ensure that our curriculum is tailored to what these companies are looking for in new hires.
Upon graduation, our students have a strong network of contacts, valuable skills, and a personal portfolio of media projects to showcase their abilities.
If you’re a creative individual who’s ready to learn the skills you need to succeed in the industry, apply now for our Year 10, Year 12 or Year 14 courses starting in September.
Where Are They Now?
Graduates of Global Academy have gained employment with some of the most renowned media companies in the world, including Global, Facebook, TikTok, Google, and the BBC.

pageCache.text:
PSHE and British Values @ Global Academy
PSHE @ Global Academy empowers students with vital skills and knowledge through diverse themes, promoting well-being, inclusion, and personal development for life beyond school.
Personal, Social, Health, and Economic Education (PSHE) is an essential part of the school curriculum – known as Global Cultural Learning – that focuses on equipping students with the knowledge, skills, and attributes they need to thrive in life in the media and entertainment industry.
At Global Academy, we cover a large variety of themes from KS4 through to KS5. These themes include;
At Global Academy, we support students with a range of health and well-being initiatives through our Global Cultural Learning lessons, Pastoral Care Leads, School Councillor, and G:fit programme. Our varied personal development programme offers Key Stage 4 and Key Stage 5 students activities tailored to their individual needs, interests, and ambitions, preparing them for long-lasting careers in the creative media sector through careers guidance, academic and personal mentoring, SEND support, and more!
We use a variety of digital platforms such as Wellio education, Unifrog and PSHE association. Here at Global Academy we also use external agencies, guest speakers and our DE&I strategy to deliver our PSHE sessions.
Key Stage 4 GCL is delivered through lessons, Network meetings, enrichment activities, themed assemblies, and targeted workshops. These lessons help young people develop as individuals and community members.
Facilitated by teaching staff, pastoral staff, and external agencies – the curriculum shapes students into responsible, respectful, enterprising citizens who positively impact society by understanding British values, equality, diversity, and inclusion. It celebrates commonalities and respects protected characteristics as defined by law. G:CL also builds essential soft skills like resilience, confidence, and independence, and promotes physical and mental health.
Key Stage 5 GCL is delivered once a week as a discrete lesson, supporting studens to be conscientious, respectful, and active citizens. The curriculum covers equality, diversity, inclusion, health, and the consequences of risky behaviors like unprotected sex, substance abuse, and crime. Students learn to handle media pressures, manage personal finances, and cope with stress during exams and final major projects, preparing students for apprenticeships, University, or work in industry. Sessions also address Relationships and Sex Education and Health Education.

British Values
Global Academy is a unique school because students from a wide variety of communities join the school, including London, Berkshire, and the South East. As a diverse community, we are dedicated to providing a range of opportunities that enable all of our students to kickstart their careers in the creative industry and become active citizens in the world. We believe that in order to prepare our learners for life in modern Britain – the role of ensuring that we promote British values to our students is paramount. The government set out its definition of British values in the 2011 Prevent Strategy and these were reinforced in 2014.
The British values are:
See below on how we are integrating Fundamental British Values into everyday life at Global Academy:
Democracy
The rule of Law
Individual liberty
Democracy
At Global Academy, we are committed to fostering an inclusive and fair environment for all students, in line with the values of the media and entertainment industry. This includes promoting equal opportunities, safeguarding rights, and encouraging active participation in decision-making processes. We believe that everyone has a role to play in shaping the future of our industry and that respecting democratic principles is essential for success in the creative sector.
Global Academy will achieve this by:
Empowering the “Student Voice”: Students are actively involved in shaping their learning environment and experiences, taking part in focus groups to provide feedback on the Academy’s strengths and areas for improvement.
Involving Students in Recruitment: Students participate in discussions and panels related to the recruitment of staff, reflecting the collaborative culture of the media and entertainment industry.
Hosting Discussions and Debates: Personal, Health, and Social Education (PHSE) lessons include debates and cultural discussions, encouraging critical thinking and communication skills vital for careers in media.
Welcoming Industry Experts: Guest speakers and workshops provide students with exposure to diverse perspectives, broadening their understanding of the ever-evolving media and entertainment landscape.
Supporting Charitable Initiatives: Fundraising efforts for causes such as Global’s Make Some Noise teach students the importance of social responsibility and community impact within the industry.
Building Partnerships: Regular meetings between the Student Leadership Team, Senior Leadership Team, governing body, and industry partners ensure that student voices shape the Academy’s direction, mirroring real-world collaboration.
Celebrating Achievements: Special assemblies recognise student accomplishments, fostering a culture of encouragement and celebration similar to industry award ceremonies.
Ensuring Equal Opportunities in Learning: Differentiated lessons and ongoing staff training ensure that students with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) are supported in reaching their creative potential.
Through these initiatives, Global Academy not only prepares students for successful careers in media and entertainment but also instils values of fairness, respect, and active participation that are fundamental to a thriving democratic society.
The Rule of the Law
At Global Academy, we prepare students for the media and entertainment industry by fostering a deep understanding of the rule of law. This includes recognising that everyone must follow the law, take responsibility for their actions, treat others fairly, and protect the rights of all. These principles are essential for building trust and accountability in the professional world.
Global Academy will achieve this by:
Home-School Agreement: Establishing a mutual understanding between the Academy, students, and their families, ensuring clarity about roles and responsibilities in maintaining a respectful and productive learning environment.
Behaviour and Rewards System: Implementing a structured system to encourage positive behaviour and celebrate achievements, helping to create an atmosphere of fairness and mutual respect, essential for collaborative success in the media industry.
Understanding Laws and Regulations: Providing Global Cultural Learning lessons where students explore how laws are made and applied, emphasising the importance of equality and fairness in society and the workplace.
Promoting Ethical Values: Actively promoting respect and ethical decision-making, helping students understand the difference between right and wrong—an essential foundation for professional integrity.
Consistent Behaviour Management: Maintaining a clear and consistent behaviour management system that ensures fairness and accountability, mirroring the standards required for professional conduct in media environments.
Highlighting the Importance of Rules: Regularly reinforcing the significance of rules and laws in the Academy, the workplace, and society during lessons, assemblies, and when addressing behavioural concerns.
Collaborating with Local Authorities and Industry Partners: Partnering with organisations such as the Police Service and industry professionals to provide real-world insights into maintaining safety, security, and ethical standards in the media and entertainment sector.
By embedding the rule of law into our teaching and practices, Global Academy equips students with the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the legal and ethical frameworks of the media and entertainment industry, fostering responsibility and respect for all.
Individual Liberty
At Global Academy, we prepare students for the media and entertainment industry by promoting the importance of individual liberty. This value encompasses personal freedoms and rights, such as the freedom to express ideas, collaborate creatively, and practise beliefs without fear of discrimination. It also emphasises the right to live without being treated unfairly or harmed for who you are or what you believe.
Global Academy will achieve this by:
Cultivating a Creative and Inclusive Culture: We foster an environment that reflects industry standards, focusing on respect, tolerance, and resilience—key attributes for thriving in media and entertainment.
Engaging in Constructive Conversations: Our teachers guide students in understanding the importance of making informed and ethical choices within a secure and supportive setting.
Encouraging Awareness of Rights: Students are supported in becoming aware of and exercising their rights and personal freedoms, preparing them for responsible participation in professional and societal settings.
Zero Tolerance for Bullying: We ensure a safe and respectful environment by addressing any instances of bullying swiftly and effectively, creating a space where creativity can flourish.
Promoting Independence: Students are encouraged to develop independence by taking ownership of their learning, with dedicated time in lessons to work autonomously—mirroring the self-directed approach needed in the industry.
Instilling Responsibility: Students are motivated to take responsibility for their actions and are supported in making safe and ethical choices that foster personal and professional growth.
Providing Tailored Support: Vulnerable students receive focused support to help them make informed decisions, with staff always prioritising the students’ best interests in guiding their choices.
Embedding Liberty into the Curriculum: Employability skills such as problem-solving, resilience, self-management, and organisation are integrated into lessons, preparing students to navigate the creative sector confidently and responsibly.
By embedding the principles of individual liberty into our culture and curriculum, Global Academy equips students with the confidence and capability to express themselves, collaborate, and succeed in the dynamic world of media and entertainment.
Mutual Respect and Tolerance
At Global Academy, we uphold the British values of mutual respect and tolerance, which are essential for fostering a harmonious and inclusive society. These principles are especially critical in the media and entertainment industry, where diverse perspectives and collaboration are key to success. Respecting all cultures, religions, and beliefs, while being open-minded to differing viewpoints, prepares students for a future where creativity thrives on understanding and cooperation.
Global Academy will achieve this by:
Embedding Respect in Our Ethos: Respect is at the core of our creative industry ethos. Students are expected to demonstrate respect towards adults, peers, and industry partners, reflecting professional standards.
Exploring Respect Through Assemblies and Talks: Assemblies and gTalks provide opportunities to explore the meaning of respect and its application in daily life, both personally and professionally.
Emphasising Respect in Behaviour: Our Behaviour Policy reinforces the importance of respect in classrooms and across all Academy activities, setting clear expectations for conduct.
Celebrating Diversity: Students gain a deep understanding and appreciation for diverse cultures and ways of life, essential for thriving in a globalised creative industry.
Encouraging Healthy Debates: Classroom discussions foster respectful dialogue and resilience, teaching students to appreciate differing viewpoints while confidently expressing their own.
Addressing Discrimination: Staff and students are encouraged to challenge prejudicial or discriminatory behaviour, with incidents being recorded and addressed in alignment with our commitment to inclusivity.
Reflecting Diversity in Media: Our Youths Choice and The Loop presenters represent the diverse makeup of the Global Academy community, showcasing inclusivity in action.
Fostering Tolerance of Faiths and Beliefs:
Curriculum Focus: English and media topics are carefully selected to spark discussions on prejudice, discrimination, and cultural understanding. For example, this Autumn Term includes a focus on Windrush to deepen students’ historical and cultural knowledge.
Global Cultural Learning Lessons: Religious Education is integrated into our curriculum, providing insights into various belief systems and practices.
Industry Partnerships: Collaborations with partners like Canon EMEA during National Inclusion Week reinforce the importance of respecting and understanding diverse perspectives.
Celebration Events: Unique events such as Black History Month, Diwali, and Pride promote awareness and tolerance, reflecting the vibrant diversity of the Global Academy community.
By integrating mutual respect and tolerance into our culture and curriculum, Global Academy prepares students to succeed in the dynamic and inclusive media and entertainment industry, where collaboration and understanding are key.

Careers and Personal Development
Global Academy places huge importance on careers education and personal development for all students during their time at the Academy to prepare them for long lasting careers in the creative industry.
Kickstart Your Career in Media & Entertainment
At Global Academy, we equip students with the practical skills, knowledge, and contacts needed for successful careers in the media and entertainment industry.
Our vision is simple; to prepare students not just academically but also to be ‘industry-ready’ for careers in media and entertainment.
Our Careers and Personal Development programme is centred on our four key values: Think Big, Keep it Simple, Own It, and Better Together.
Our broad and balanced curriculum emphasises Personal Development and Careers Education, focusing on key qualities such as resilience, confidence, and ambition—essential attributes for thriving in a fast-paced environment. Students not only gain industry-specific skills but also develop self-awareness and personal responsibility. By setting high expectations for conduct, we prepare them to be well-rounded citizens ready for the industry. Graduates leave the Academy equipped for employment, further education, or training in the creative industry.
At Global Academy, Personal Development and Careers Education are integral to our approach, empowering students to confidently pursue their ambitions and make a meaningful impact in the media and entertainment landscape.

pageCache.text:
Alumni
Discover where Global Academy graduates thrive in media and entertainment careers.
Destinations at Global
Global Academy equips students for careers in media and entertainment, as well as further education and training. Explore our graduates’ diverse career paths and destinations. Explore where Global Academy students go after graduation below for career, education, and training paths in media and entertainment:
90%
of our graduates are working or training in the Creative Industries.
Industry-Ready Graduates
At Global Academy, we are dedicated to preparing our pupils for long-lasting careers in the dynamic and ever-evolving Media and Entertainment industry. Our unique approach, grounded in our core values of “Think big”, “Keep it simple”, “Own it”, and “Better together”, ensures that our graduates are not just academically proficient, but truly industry-ready.
Powering the Creative Industries
Our comprehensive curriculum, developed in close collaboration with leading industry professionals, equips our pupils with the technical skills, vocational knowledge, and academic excellence required to thrive in this fast-paced sector. As a result, 90% of our graduates are working or training in the Creative Industries – a testament to the effectiveness of our approach.
Destinations of Distinction
Our most recent graduates have secured employment and apprenticeships at some of the most prestigious media companies in the world, including Global, BBC, Sky, TikTok, Facebook, Google, Dentsu, Mediacom, NBC Universal, Pinewood Studios, News UK, and Premier League Productions. This impressive track record directly reflects our unwavering commitment to “Think big” and deliver an exceptional educational experience.
In addition to these industry-leading destinations, our pupils have also been accepted into top universities, such as London College of Communication, Pearson College: Escape Studios, University of Kent, and University of the Arts London. These prestigious institutions provide our graduates with the opportunity to further develop their skills and knowledge, ensuring they are well-equipped to become the next generation of leaders in the creative sector.
Empowering the Next Generation
At Global Academy, we take great pride in our ability to transform ambitious young minds into industry-ready professionals. By “Keeping it simple” and maintaining a relentless focus on academic excellence, vocational training, and technical skill development, we are able to “Own it” and deliver outstanding outcomes for our pupils. Through our “Better together” approach, we continue to forge strong partnerships with industry partners, ensuring that our curriculum remains relevant, dynamic, and responsive to the evolving needs of the media and entertainment industries.
Alumni Stories
Krystal D'Anjou
Krystal graduated in 2020 and has an exciting career in the industry since leaving the Academy working with some of the world’s biggest brands and publishers.
She left the Academy and landed a position with Global’s video team as an Apprentice creating content and generating creative ideas for their radio brands – after Global, she has worked with a wide range of brands and publishers including EUEFA, Adidas, Red Bull, Dr Martens, Nike, Puma and many more.
Krystal currently runs her own popular Instagram and Tiktok channel as well as being Head of TikTok for Gen Z publishers – Guap as well as having her own YouTube shows “Boujee on a Budget” and “Dusk2Dawn”
Jack Payne
Jack joined our Level 4 course in 2023 and was selected to win the RTS Craft Award for Editing in the Student Television Awards.
Since graduating – Jack has landed a role as Production Runner on BBC’s Eastenders where he plays a crucial role in supporting the production team to ensure smooth and efficient operations on set. This role involves a variety of tasks, including coordinating logistics, assisting with set preparation, and providing general support to the cast and crew.
Ariana Crossdale
After studying at Global Academy, Ariana Crosdale wasted no time in joining the industry! Now a Junior Producer, Ariana says “Global Academy gave me tons of hands-on experience in content creation and digital marketing, giving me the skills needed to excel in my role. The collaborative projects and real-world assignments helped me develop a strong understanding of industry standards and best practices. Additionally, the guidance and mentorship from experienced professionals at the Academy were invaluable in building my confidence and professional network.”
Ariana works at a company called Viator, who are owned by TripAdvisor. With a busy schedule, Ariana says her day-to-day role includes, “Creating content for all aspects of the business, such as ads, social media, and internal communications. This may involve assisting with a banner for a Google ad one day and producing videos for the Viator website the next. Also, I collaborate closely with different departments to ensure messaging is consistent and engaging, often participating in brainstorming sessions to develop innovative marketing strategies through content.”
Ariella Vana
Ariella Vana graduated in 2023 and landed a role as a Digital Content Apprentice at Heart.
This has helped kickstart an exciting digital career after the Academy. She’s been hands-on in major projects like Global’s Make Some Noise Day, filming with stars like Perrie and Kylie, and even interviewing Andrew Garfield at the London Film Festival.
Ariella says: “The skills and connections I made at Global Academy have truly set me up for this role.”
Pedro Teixeira
Pedro graduated from Global Academy and has since enrolled in the Level 4 Course at Creative Media Institute/Amersham College, in partnership with Pinewood Studios. He created a stunning public exhibition featuring cyanotype prints and still life photography, which was showcased at The Autograph Art Gallery.
In recognition of his talent, his work was also selected for display on the renowned Old Street Digital Canvas billboard in London. Pedro’s journey exemplifies the creative and professional opportunities available to Global Academy graduates as they pursue their passions in the media and arts.
Ellie Vesey
After two years in our Sixth Form, Ellie Vesey graduated and is looking forward to starting her exclusive apprenticeship with Global in September 2024.
As the new Brand Experience Apprentice, Ellie says she will take part in, “shaping the customer experience and linking it back to the company through the use of events, and our trusted partnerships who work alongside us.”
“Global Academy helped prepare me for working life in so many different ways, but mainly the constant work experience and opportunities that I was given, which helped me to understand the industry that I would be joining once I finished Sixth Form.”
Ronnie Koldashi
Ronnie Koldashi, a Global Academy graduate, has turned his passion for property and marketing into a dream career as Head of Marketing for Savoys Properties.
During his time in Year 14 – he established a contact for the company and did a work placement with them. Ronnie impressed the owners so much that they offered him a job there and then and he worked up to a senior position within 12 months.
In this role, he creates high-end promotional content, websites, and digital assets, showcasing luxury properties.
His journey reflects the valuable skills and experiences gained at Global Academy in content creation, marketing and entrepreneurship – paving the way for success in the competitive real estate market.
Liberty Hosgood
Liberty Hosgood is now a Media Executive in Global’s national commercial team, where she plans, buys, and manages hundreds of commercial audio advertising campaigns each year.
After leaving Global Academy, she attended the University of West London to complete her BA in Media and Communications, along with a short stint in Global Academy’s Marketing and Outreach team.
Liberty has also freelanced, producing her own short documentary and producing interviews on the popular “BrunchWithAmel” podcast and video series.
Here, she participates in Global’s annual charity fundraising day for Make Some Noise, as shown by her outfit!
Stanley Thompson and George Buckley
Global Academy 2023 graduate’s Stanley Thompson and George Buckley have begun their careers in video editing.
Stanley and George now work as Video Editors at The Fellas Studios.
D'Angelo Briscoe
D’Angelo Briscoe graduated from Global Academy and after his apprenticeship, landed a full time role at Capital FM as an Assistant Sound Designer!

Apprenticeships
What are your options if you’re thinking of an Apprenticeship?
Thinking of taking an Apprenticeship after Global Academy?
Another option for students who graduate from Global Academy is an Apprenticeship. Apprenticeships involve taking on a real job with responsibilities, whilst studying towards a recognised qualification and getting paid too!
What are Apprenticeships?
Apprenticeships are ideal if you have a clear idea of the career you’d like to pursue, and you’re willing to commit to work and study. Students can undertake an apprenticeship when they finish at Global Academy instead of going to University. The majority of your learning will be through on-the-job training in your place of work.
This is a great option if you want to specialise in a certain area of the industry after you’ve completed your studies at Global Academy.
There are different types of Apprenticeships that lead to different levels of qualification:
Whichever level you start on, you’ll be gaining valuable on-the-job experience alongside recognised learning. Depending on which career route you’re planning to take, choosing an Apprenticeship might just be the best option for you.
Find out more by checking out the following links:

Our job is to get you a job!
Careers and Industry Programme at Global Academy
Global Academy prides itself on preparing our students for long lasting careers in the creative media industry – our job is to get them a job!
Global Academy aims to equip students with both the practical and soft skills required for a career in the creative media industry. The creative industry is the UK’s fastest-growing economy, making up one in every eleven jobs. The creative industries are worth £115 billion a year to the UK economy, larger than the automotive, aerospace, life sciences, oil and gas industries combined. And they are growing faster than the rest of the UK economy.
The Global Academy careers programme sets out how the Academy intends to provide a fit-for-purpose careers programme with the available resources which will provide our students with the knowledge, inspiration and ability to take ownership of their own career action plans which will enable them to succeed in their chosen career paths.
We measure the success of our careers programme by the destinations students reach after leaving the Global Academy in Year 13 who land roles in top media companies like Global, the BBC, Google, TikTok, Bloomberg and more – as well as leading advertising agencies like Dentsu, Ogilvy and Mediacom.
Careers and Industry is embedded in everything we do at Global Academy – having industry guests, creative sector partnerships or career-related activity across the school is almost a daily occurrence. Our most recent Ofsted report praised our unique approach to careers and industry:
Excellent careers advice and guidance from a range of personnel, including from the creative media industry, colleges and universities, contribute to an impressive number of pupils making the transition to further education, employment or training. Almost all Year 11 pupils and Year 13 students, including disadvantaged pupils, secured employment, education or training that met their needs and interests.
Students benefit from strong preparation for their future careers. For example, they receive individual mentoring from specialists from the creative media industry, as well as bespoke support and guidance from a range of colleges, universities and apprenticeship providers.
Careers Access Policy and Global Academy's Careers Plan
Click here to read our Careers Programme Guides, Careers Policy, Careers Progression Framework and Careers Access Policy
Key Contacts
SLT Link for Careers and Personal Development - Jonathan Jacob
Our Careers Leader is Jonathan Jacob –Assistant Principal, who is the SLT member responsible and has an overall strategic overview for Global Academy’s career provision, employer engagement, careers education and specialist media curriculum and training.
Careers and Industry Partnerships Director - Shahlaa Tahira
Shahlaa is our dedicated Careers and Industry Partnerships Lead, specialising in forging strong connections between our students and the creative media sector. With a focus on creating valuable opportunities and experiences, Shahlaa works tirelessly to ensure students gain essential industry exposure and build crucial networks. Her efforts are instrumental in developing a seamless pipeline that helps graduates secure exciting roles in the creative media industry.
Careers Link Governor - Desaray Ellis
Enterprise Advisor - Glen Funnell
Glen Funnell- Co-Founder & Executive Producer of Hatch Films is the Global Academy Enterprise Advisor who works closely with Global Academy to provide an external strategic focus to ensure Global Academy delivers quality careers and employer-focused education.
Their volunteer provision is provided via the West London Career Hub and is supported by the London Enterprise Advisor Network / Mayor of London.
Careers Advisor - Karen Medina
Karen works with Global Academy students to provide 1:1 careers guidance for our students to help them progress into the next stage of their careers. Contact Karen to book your appointment.
Careers at Global Academy
Global Academy places huge importance on Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) for all students during their time at the Academy as the ambition for the Global Academy is prepare young people for successful careers in the creative media industry.
The Global Academy Careers Plan sets out how the school intends to provide a fit for purpose careers programme with the available resources which will provide our students with the knowledge, inspiration and ability to take ownership of their own career action plans which will enable them to succeed in their chosen creative career paths.
As well as our careers education, information, advice and guidance; our industry-focused media curriculum means students are more creative, more intellectually curious and (critically) more likely to demonstrate the skill set required to impress universities and top creative industry employers.
Regular reflection across the course of study allows students to quantify their experience, learning and understanding to help prepare them for the industry.
This means that our students leave the Academy and go in to employment, education or further training with knowledge, experience and focus – especially within the creative and broadcast industries. We want to ensure that all students are well prepared for whatever they decide to do after their time at the Academy whether this be further education, employment or further training.
Our policy ensure that all learners are exposed to experiences to help shape their journey after the Academy. In short – during their Global Academy two or four year journey we can ensure our students are given the insight, skills and resources to get them to the top of their game within a media and creative industry career.
Careers is embedded through the formal taught academic curriculum where appropriate. Each subject area includes links appropriate careers and life skills built into their schemes of learning and students are taught about opportunities for employment based on the skills they learn. Students are involved in the evaluation of activities; feedback is collated and fed in to the Careers development plan and the overall school development plan.
Discover, Inspire, Progress
Our programme of careers interventions are designed through a delivery framework of Discover, Inspire and Progress

External opportunities are advertised
Our Approach and Vision
The Academy aims to equip students with both the practical and soft skills required for a career in the creative media industry. The creative industry is the UK’s fastest growing economy:
1 in 8 businesses in the UK are part of the creative industries.
In 2021, the creative industries contributed £109bn to the UK economy – this was 5.6% of the economy in that year!
The biggest contributor of the 12 subsectors was IT, software and computer services which contributed 2.3% to the UK economy.
The UK government has announced plans to add 50bn in value to the Creative Industries by 2025 …growing the sector by a third!
As well as the importance to the UK economy – we place a value on CEAIG (Careers Education, Advice, Information & Guidance) to help deliver social mobility and to open doors for all young people. The government has recently endorsed the fact that “great careers guidance provides the first rung on the ladder of opportunity, helping everyone to achieve their full potential”. (DfE, 2017, p.3).
Alongside our careers education, information, advice and guidance; our industry focused media curriculum means students are more creative, more intellectually curious and (critically) more likely to demonstrate the skill set required to impress universities and top creative industry employers. Regular reflection across the course of study allows students to quantify their experience, learning and understanding to help prepare them for the industry.
We work closely with our industry partners, Global and the wider media community to ensure our practical and vocational education reflects both the practical and soft skills required for long lasting employment. This is delivered through the practical media curriculum across all levels of the school. Alongside the media curriculum, further preparation for a career in the media industry is installed within our learners through a varied and customised programme of workshops, electives, guest speakers, enrichment and work experience.
We want to ensure that all students are well prepared for whatever they decide to do after their time at the Academy whether this be further education, employment or further training. Our policy ensures that learners are exposed to experiences to help shape their journey after the Academy. In short, during their Global Academy journey, we can ensure our students are given the insight, skills and resources to get them to the top of their game within a media and creative industry career.
What Happens?
The operational delivery of Careers and Employability at the Academy is delivered through the eight key pillars of the Gatsby Benchmarks:

2. Learning from Career & Labour Market Information
3. Addressing the Needs of Each Pupil
4. Linking Curriculum Learning to Careers
5. Encounters with Employers & Employees
6. Experiences of Workplaces

Need Advice?
Here’s where you can get advice and guidance on your next steps
Guidance for Students and Parents
If you or your child would like to receive advice on future careers and plans for after they finish at Global Academy please contact your Form Tutor or Media Mentor in the first instance.
All our students are entitled to a 1-to-1 personal guidance appointment with Karen (qualified careers). Guidance interviews are an opportunity for the student to explore career ideas and aspirations, discuss progression routes, as well as address any barriers they might be facing and receive information and advice that is tailored to their interests. A personal guidance interview is a confidential opportunity for the student to speak to a trained guidance counsellor, as such parents and carers are not usually invited to attend this interview.
Students can also book a meeting with our Careers Advisor, Karen Medina – via Karen.Medina@globalacademy.com
Students can access a range of physical resources and guides via the “Careers Office” in the LRC as well as via Canvas and Unifrog.
Remember to check out the careers notice boards and weekly careers newsletter for apprenticeships, universities, FE opportunities and other information on the ground floor and the second floor.
The ERIC app is a free careers app helping you break into the creative industries and become work-ready. Browse thousands of internships, events, training schemes, courses and more.
Simply download the app, tell us about your creative interests & location, and the app will match you to opportunities & experiences in your area.
The National Careers Service
The National Careers Service offers free impartial careers advice to help individuals make informed decisions about their careers, education training and employment opportunities. They offer help and advice on CVs and job interviews, choosing a course, applying for further or higher education, making overseas qualifications count, applying for jobs or deciding on a career direction. They also offer:
• Assistance with producing a winning CV
• Professional advice on job search techniques
• Advice on filling in application forms
• Interview practice
• Guidance on voluntary work
Unifrog
Unifrog is an online platform that supports schools and colleges to deliver their statutory duty to provide students with impartial and independent guidance on the full range of Post-16 and Post-18 options.
Unifrog is the only place where students can compare every undergraduate course in the UK as well as international opportunities. Additionally, Unifrog provides students with access to the most comprehensive list of live apprenticeships available across the country including Higher, SLP and degree apprenticeships, as well as FE courses.
Once students have explored their interests and compared the full range of pathways available to them, Unifrog provides one place for students to draft all materials needed for applications such as CVs and Personal Statements.
All students, across all year groups, now have access to the platform in keeping with our commitment to provide students with outstanding careers guidance and tailored support when choosing their next step.
Benefits for teachers
Unifrog is a whole-school careers platform. It allows teachers and careers advisors to track their pupils’ progress and keep a record of their research and all of the careers interactions each student has received. It makes it easy for teachers and careers advisors to work with students to find the best next step for them. Staff are able to provide feedback on applications, comment on students’ research, log careers interviews and interactions as well as upload action plans, and provide support and feedback on application materials. Information for parents and carers
Every parent/carer can have their own login to Unifrog, where they can access the tools, information, and guidance to support their child to make their best next step. Contact a member of the Careers Team to receive your unique login for Unifrog, and receive support on how to navigate the Unifrog platform.
Other Sources of Guidance for Parents
Talking Futures is a recommended website for parents to have informed and constructive conversations with your child about training and education using the Talking Futures toolkit – talkingfutures.org.uk
WonderWhat App
WonderWhat is a free web app where career advice meets creativity
Created for ages 13+, simply tap on images you like, and it will match-make you with 3 creative career options.
It will show you realtime sector salary information, the freshest news, and social accounts you should follow.
Prefer to type? They’ve trained a Chat GPT model based on a carefully curated course dataset to recommend careers based on what you tell us you like, or – if you know what subject you’re interested in, go straight there.

University
If you’re looking to continue your education after the Academy, then you may well be thinking of going on to University
Thinking About University?
If you’re looking to continue your education after the Academy, then you may well be thinking of going on to University. This could give you an employability advantage too, especially if you’re going to be studying an industry-relevant subject with high technical content.
Not all, but a lot of employers these days are looking for a degree-level education so a few years at University could very well get your foot in quite a few more doors in the future.
Preparation for University
We know that for many, going to University is a big, personal step and that’s something we’re really keen to help make a seamless process. Although we’re committed to high-quality learning and you passing our course, we’ll ensure that you grow as the individual you are as well.
After all, many employers take personal growth into account when they’re recruiting, so we’ll actively encourage you to throw yourself into our range of projects and opportunities which will hone some essential life skills and enable you to work with a wide range of people in the future – all whilst making the move to University less daunting!
Support
Whilst you’re here at Global Academy, we’ll take the time to get to know you and your personal ambitions. We’ll encourage you to think about who, what, and where you want to be in life and back you all the way

Discover our partners at Global Academy
Making Learning Real
Global Academy have worked with a huge host of media brands, companies and partners to give students real-life experience of the Broadcast and Digital Media Industry.
If you’re interested in working with our students to develop your talent pipeline, please contact Assistant Principal, Jonathan Jacob.
Global
Global is one of the world’s leading Media & Entertainment groups. With a huge weekly reach, it is the UK and Europe’s largest Radio & Outdoor company.
Global is home to respected, national, market leading media brands including Capital, Heart, Classic FM, LBC, Global’s Newsroom, Smooth, Radio X, Capital XTRA, Gold and Global Player, which allows listeners to enjoy all of Global’s radio brands, award-winning podcasts, and expertly-curated playlists, in one place in app, on web and on smart speakers.
With an extensive and diverse portfolio, Global is also the leading Outdoor company in the UK & one of the largest in Europe with over 235,000 sites reaching 95% of the UK population.
On-air, on Global Player and with our outdoor platforms combined, Global reaches 51 million individuals across the UK every week, including 26.3 million on the radio alone.
Global created and operates DAX, the market leader in Digital audio advertising. Through its proprietary technology, DAX connects advertisers with an audience of more than 130 million people worldwide, inserting targeted advertising into music streaming services, connected radio listening and podcasts in the UK, Europe, the USA and Canada. DAX is the largest digital audio advertising platform in the UK and one of the largest in the world.
The company headquarters is in London’s iconic Leicester Square. Ashley Tabor-King CBE is Founder & Executive President, Simon Pitts is Group CEO, Stephen Miron is Chairman and James Rea is Chief Broadcasting & Content Officer. Ashley Tabor-King created Global in 2007.
100+ alumni have been employed by Global since 2018
UAL: London College of Communication
UAL: London College of Communication
University of the Arts London (UAL) is a world-leading university for art and design (ranked second in the world for Art and Design in the 2021 QS World University Rankings®) and the founding educational partner of Global Academy.
UAL’s London College of Communication works right alongside the Global Academy team to deliver an amazing educational experience that will set students up for long-term success in the creative industries, with students studying a leading qualification from the UAL awarding body.
A global pioneer in creative communications education, London College of Communication is for the curious, the brave and the committed: those who want to transform themselves and the world around them.
The College works at the cutting edge of new thinking in Design, Media and Screen to discover new possibilities in creative communications and prepare its students to succeed as future-facing creatives.
Baker Dearing Educational Trust
Global Academy is a UTC (University Technical College) school and supported by the Baker Dearing Educational Trust.
Baker Dearing Educational Trust was founded by Lord Baker and Lord Dearing to develop and promote the concept of university technical colleges. Today they are a small, flexible organisation that sits at the centre of the UTC network. Their focus is on promoting and supporting new and existing UTCs like Global Academy.
“The UK needs advanced technical skills at all levels if we are to prosper in the 21st century. Whether in manufacturing, wind farms, rail links or hi-tech hospitals we need a workforce that can develop new products, stretch and reuse existing resources and meet all the challenges of the future.”
Lord Baker, Chairman
University Technical Colleges (UTCs) are government-funded schools that offer 14–18 year olds a great deal more than traditional schools. They teach students technical subjects in a whole new way and are educating the inventors, programmers, developers, engineers, and technicians of tomorrow.
UTCs integrate technical, practical and academic learning and create an environment where students can thrive and develop the abilities that tomorrow’s industries will need.

pageCache.pageTitle: Graduate Does Sound Design at Capital FM – Global Academy School and Sixth Form in London
pageCache.text:
25 November 2020
Graduate Does Sound Design at Capital FM
From Global Academy to Capital FM
D’Angelo joined the Academy and immediately took a great interest in audio. He impressed his audio teachers and produced some great audio projects. Whilst at the Academy he gained many insights into the industry. At the end of his time, he was offered an apprenticeship with Capital FM to be a Broadcast Assistant. He excelled through his apprenticeship and was offered a full time position as Assistant Sound Designer at Capital!
Read on to see more about D’Angelo’s work at Capital and how Global Academy prepared him for his career in the industry
Working at Capital FM
D’Angelo said “During my time as an apprentice I was able to do all the roles that are required by Capital to work behind the scenes. As an apprentice I was able to produce a number of shows including The Capital Late Show with Marvin Humes”
“As I’m a DJ, I was able to use that knowledge to help create mixes for The Capital Weekender and now Capital Dance. Lastly, I was able to make all the production that goes out on air – jingles, branded intros, promos, montages, sponsorships and many more which I now do in my current role.”
How Did Global Academy Help You?
I’ve never encountered a school that has truly encouraged and pushed me into what I wanted to do. I came out with experience, connections and a career that was a childhood dream!
I was able to be part of Youths Choice which helped me understand the type of audience we should be aiming for, the sound of the station and create jingles, sweepers and montages which is what I do now just on a larger scale. It allowed me to learn software e.g. Pro Tools, Adobe Audition and Zetta, a new piece of broadcasting software that is now being pushed throughout most of the radio stations here at global.
I came out of Global Academy with experience, connections and a career that was a childhood dream!
What Advice Would You Give to a Global Academy Student?
Be an opportunist. I travelled over 1 hour and 30mins, made new friend and most importantly made every day count that I went to the Global Academy, which then helped me get an apprenticeship and now a full time job.
Be different. Take part in everything that Global Academy offers and do more. Whether that’s staying late to practise in the radio/TV studios or show people what makes you unique.
Have a want to mindset. You need to go in everyday knowing that if you put your all in you will get something out of it. If the teachers can see it, your friends can see it, it’ll help you see it.

pageCache.pageTitle: Graduate Lands Apprenticeship at BBC – Global Academy School and Sixth Form in London
pageCache.text:
11 November 2020
Graduate Lands Apprenticeship at BBC
Read how Narveer Toor landed her dream role at the BBC after graduating from Global Academy!
Working at the BBC
My first job after leaving Global Academy will be as a Digital Marketer Apprentice at the BBC and I am very excited to get a real sense of what marketing is like in a big corporation. I’m moving to Manchester for the experience and can’t wait!
Always go the extra mile
Why did you choose Global Academy?
For me media has always been a passion from a young age! When finding out about the Global Academy, and learning what they do; which is teaching practical skills to aspiring students – I knew that this was place that I wanted to join!
How did Global Academy help prepare you for your new role?
The Academy handed me the tools that I need to succeed in marketing. For example they informed me what companies look for and how to present yourselves within your portfolio and CV’s. In addition to this, the Academy really pushed me to do extra projects outside of school. This not only looks impressive on your CV but also enables you to improve on my skill set.
What advice would you give to students following in your footsteps?
Always go the extra mile. No matter what project you are working on, even if its a subject that you’re not keen on. People will note this behaviour, thus giving you a good reputation. I would also recommend to always be working on a side project. I say this because it adds depth into what you do and shows that you aren’t just doing the bare minimum at school, but that you are passionate about the career you want to get into.

pageCache.pageTitle: Graduate Works for Premier League Productions – Global Academy School and Sixth Form in London
pageCache.text:
24 November 2020
Graduate Works for Premier League Productions
Media Coordinator at Premier League Productions
Lily Ledworth landed the role Media Coordinator at Premier League Productions after graduating from the Global Academy. Working in Sports TV she often has to coordinate live events and work under pressure in a stadium full of people!
Working In Media
Whilst studying at Global, Lily spent many of her weekends undertaking work experience with a variety of production companies. Lily explains “I was just a spare pair of hands then as I continued to prove myself I started getting runner roles.”
When I applied for my job I had more experience than most uni graduates
Advice For Students Following in Lily’s Footsteps
Take every opportunity to do as much work experience as possible. When I applied for my job I had more experience than most uni graduates – it wasn’t handed to me I spent all of my school holidays and many weekends working on different TV shows. At first I was just a spare pair of hands but as I did it more and continued to prove myself I started getting runner roles.
Even though it’s not exactly what I’m doing in my role now. When I was at Global Academy, we kept being told it’s so important to have things on your CV – but it’s so much more than that! In my job interview I was able to list over 10 TV shows that I had worked on in previous few months. Without a doubt- it was my work experience that got me to where I am because it showed my hardworking personality and my willingness to learn.
